quote: It is not death that a man should fear, but he should fear never beginning to live.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Think of yourself as dead. You have lived your life. Now, take what's left and live it properly.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Do not act as if you were going to live ten thousand years. Death hangs over you. While you live, while it is in your power, be good.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Death is a release from the impressions of the senses, and from desires that make us their puppets, and from the vagaries of the mind, and from the hard service of the flesh.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Casting aside other things, hold to the precious few; and besides bear in mind that every man lives only the present, which is an indivisible point.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Stop whatever you're doing for a moment and ask yourself: am I afraid of death because I won't be able to do this anymore?
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Perfection of character is this: to live each day as if it were your last, without frenzy, without apathy, without pretence.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: If you are distressed by anything external, the pain is not due to the thing itself, but to your estimate of it; and this you have the power to revoke at any moment.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Everything we hear is an opinion, not a fact. Everything we see is a perspective, not the truth.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The soul becomes dyed with the colour of its thoughts.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Never let the future disturb you. You will meet it, if you have to, with the same weapons of reason which today arm you against the present.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Accept the things to which fate binds you, and love the people with whom fate brings you together, but do so with all your heart.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Adapt yourself to the life you have been given; and truly love the people with whom destiny has surrounded you.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The best revenge is to be unlike him who performed the injury.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: If it is not right do not do it; if it is not true do not say it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The object of life is not to be on the side of the majority, but to escape finding oneself in the ranks of the insane.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Say to yourself in the early morning: I shall meet today ungrateful, violent, treacherous, envious, uncharitable men. All of these things have come upon them through ignorance of real good and ill.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Like an olive that ripens and falls, praising its mother, thanking the tree it grew on, pass through this brief life as nature demands, and give it up without complaint.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Nothing that is according to nature can be evil.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: There are more things, Lucilius, likely to frighten us than there are to crush us; we suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca

quote: So it is with anger, my dear Lucilius; the outcome of a mighty anger is madness, and hence anger should be avoided, not merely that we may escape excess, but that we may have a healthy mind.
author: Seneca

quote: The greatest remedy for anger is delay.
author: Seneca

quote: It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a great deal of it.
author: Seneca

quote: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
author: Seneca

quote: True happiness is to enjoy the present, without anxious dependence upon the future.
author: Seneca

quote: The greatest blessings of mankind are within us and within our reach. A wise man is content with his lot, whatever it may be, without wishing for what he has not.
author: Seneca

quote: Freedom is not the absence of external constraints but the presence of internal discipline.
author: Seneca

quote: When men have begun to desire all things in opposition to the ways of nature, they end up by entirely abandoning the ways of nature.
author: Seneca

quote: When friendship is settled, you must trust; before friendship is formed, you must pass judgement.
author: Seneca

quote: Pleasure is a poor and petty thing. No value should be set on it.
author: Seneca

quote: By no wisdom can natural weaknesses of the body be removed. That which is implanted and inborn can be toned down by training, but not overcome.
author: Seneca

quote: We cannot forbid these feelings any more than we can summon them.
author: Seneca

quote: Conduct will not be right unless the will to act is right; for this is the source of conduct.
author: Seneca

quote: The wise person's purpose in life is not to accomplish at all hazards what they attempt, but to do everything rightly.
author: Seneca

quote: Anger, if not controlled, is more harmful than the injury that provoked it.
author: Seneca

quote: The first step to being happy is to free yourself from anger.
author: Seneca

quote: External fortune adds nothing essential to a mind at peace with itself.
author: Seneca

quote: Some things are in our control and others not. Things in our control are opinion, pursuit, desire, aversion, and, in a word, whatever are our own actions.
author: Epictetus

quote: It isn't the things themselves that disturb people, but the judgements that they form about them.
author: Epictetus

quote: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.
author: Epictetus

quote: Circumstances do not make the man; they merely reveal him to himself.
author: Epictetus

quote: Freedom is the right to live as we wish.
author: Epictetus

quote: Make the best use of what is in your power, and take the rest as it happens.
author: Epictetus

quote: I must die. Must I then die lamenting? I must be put in chains. Must I then also lament? I must go into exile. Does any man then hinder me from going with smiles and cheerfulness and contentment?
author: Epictetus

quote: Practice yourself, for heaven's sake, in little things, and thence proceed to greater.
author: Epictetus

quote: No man is free who is not master of himself.
author: Epictetus

quote: First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
author: Epictetus

quote: We suffer not from the events in our lives, but from our judgment about them.
author: Epictetus

quote: It's not what happens to you, but how you react to it that matters.
author: Epictetus

quote: The more we value things outside of our control, the less control we have.
author: Epictetus

quote: Don't set your heart on so many things, and you will get what you need.
author: Epictetus

quote: It is impossible for a man to learn what he thinks he already knows.
author: Epictetus

quote: I cannot escape death, but I can escape the fear of it.
author: Epictetus

quote: Welcome events in whichever way they happen; this is the path to peace.
author: Epictetus

quote: Lay down from this moment a certain character and pattern of behaviour for yourself, which you will preserve both alone and in company.
author: Epictetus

quote: When you relax your attention for a while, do not fancy you will recover it whenever you please; remember that because of your fault today your affairs must necessarily be in a worse condition on future occasions.
author: Epictetus

quote: A habit arises in you of not paying attention, and next a habit of deferring attention, and so you get into the habit of putting off the happy and befitting life that would enable you to live in conformity with nature.
author: Epictetus

quote: The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The mind adapts and converts to its own purposes the obstacle to our acting, and a hindrance to a given duty becomes a help, an obstacle in a given path a furtherance.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: A blazing fire makes flame and brightness out of everything that is thrown into it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Don't let your imagination be crushed by life as a whole. Don't try to picture everything bad that could possibly happen. Stick with the situation at hand, and ask, why is this so unbearable, why can't I endure it?
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Everything that happens is either endurable or not. If it's endurable, then endure it and stop complaining. If it's unendurable, then stop complaining, your destruction will mean its end as well.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: To do harm is to do yourself harm. To do an injustice is to do yourself an injustice, it degrades you.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Our actions may be impeded, but there can be no impeding our intentions or dispositions, because we can accommodate and adapt.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Did an obstacle oppose your impulse? If you started out to satisfy it without mental reservation, the obstacle is at once injurious to you as a reasonable being; but if you experience the general lot, you are not yet hurt or hindered.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: If you cancel your judgement about what seems to pain you, you yourself stand firm on surest ground.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: True happiness is to enjoy the present, without anxious dependence upon the future.
author: Seneca

quote: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
author: Seneca

quote: If you really want to escape the things that harass you, what you need is not to be in a different place but to be a different person.
author: Seneca

quote: I do not forbid you to possess wealth; I only seek to make you fearless in possessing it.
author: Seneca

quote: For the wise man regards wealth as a slave, the fool as a master.
author: Seneca

quote: My riches belong to me; you belong to your riches.
author: Seneca

quote: The happy man is he who can make a right judgment in all things: he is happy who in his present circumstances, whatever they may be, is satisfied and on friendly terms with the conditions of his life.
author: Seneca

quote: Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
author: Seneca

quote: The greatest obstacle to living is expectancy, which hangs upon tomorrow and loses today.
author: Seneca

quote: Set aside a certain number of days, during which you shall be content with the scantiest and cheapest fare, so that you may test yourself and see whether that which you feared is really a hardship.
author: Seneca

quote: Nowhere is he who is everywhere. Those who spend all their life travelling abroad end by having many acquaintances but no friends.
author: Seneca

quote: That which had made poverty a burden to us, has made riches also a burden. It matters little whether you lay a sick man on a wooden or on a golden bed, for whithersoever he be moved he will carry his malady with him.
author: Seneca

quote: It is the sign of an unstable mind not to be able to endure riches.
author: Seneca

quote: Cease to hope, and you will cease to fear.
author: Seneca

quote: He is a great man who uses earthenware dishes as if they were silver; but he is equally great who uses silver as if it were earthenware.
author: Seneca

quote: What does it matter how much a man has laid up in his safe, how large are his flocks and how fat his dividends, if he covets his neighbour's property and reckons not his past gains, but his hopes of gains to come?
author: Seneca

quote: The proper limit to wealth is, first, to have what is necessary, and second, to have what is enough.
author: Seneca

quote: Poverty does not mean the possession of little, but the non-possession of much; it is used, not of what a man has, but of what he lacks.
author: Seneca

quote: Riches puff up the spirit and beget pride; the things which are goods give us greatness of soul, but riches give us arrogance, and arrogance is nothing else than a false show of greatness.
author: Seneca

quote: Money will come of its own accord; titles will be given to you; but virtue will not fall upon you by chance.
author: Seneca

quote: Poverty, brought into conformity with the law of nature, is great wealth.
author: Seneca

quote: How much better is it to get wisdom than gold! and to get understanding rather to be chosen than silver!
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: Better it is to be of an humble spirit with the lowly, than to divide the spoil with the proud.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: He that handleth a matter wisely shall find good: and whoso trusteth in the LORD, happy is he.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: Understanding is a wellspring of life unto him that hath it: but the instruction of fools is folly.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: A wrathful man stirreth up strife: but he that is slow to anger appeaseth strife.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: The way of the slothful man is as an hedge of thorns: but the way of the righteous is made plain.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: He that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity: and the rod of his anger shall fail.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: The slothful man saith, There is a lion without, I shall be slain in the streets.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: The rich and poor meet together: the LORD is the maker of them all.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom. Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? for riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: As iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: He that is soon angry dealeth foolishly: and a man of wicked devices is hated.
author: Book of Proverbs

quote: Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.
author: Book of Proverbs
